comments.text: Hey, I know you're Norwegian and you're English is amazing (better than most native speakers), however can I just explain why the British pronunciation of Iran is grammatically correct and the American pronunciation (eye ran) is grammatically incorrect. Iceland and Ireland are both pronounced with a hard I (eye) because the E changes the sound of the I. This is why Italy, Israel and Indonesia are pronounced with a soft I, because the lack of E directly after the first letter. Therefore, with zero E in Iran and Iraq, they are pronounced with a soft I like Italy. Americans constantly pronounce everything incorrectly because they don't follow basic English grammar. I wish people would stop bowing to the Americans every time they say something differently (e.g. everyone using the word "soccer" when we've all been using the word "football" for centuries).
